findings.detail: The committed manifest records `head 913d1e78…` (HEAD~1) and `findings critical=0 high=2`, `verdict REQUEST_CHANGES`. Both halves of `verify-evidence.mjs` therefore fail at HEAD 68b3aed. (1) Rule 3, content binding: I resolved the blobs and they have moved — `scripts/lib/evidence.mjs` attested `33a06f2b…` but is `702e44c7…` at HEAD; `scripts/verify-evidence.mjs` `b723c409…` → `62c3fda8…`; `scripts/attest-review.mjs` `bbf4352f…` → `35a90226…`; `tests/unit/evidence.test.ts` `121c30dd…` → `02ef84f1…`; `.apexyard/review.json` `c9a8db81…` → `470e8959…`. Each becomes a "changed after it was reviewed" problem. (2) `gateSatisfied(fields, 'high')` emits "2 unresolved high finding(s)", so the gate rule fails too. The manifest also lists `.apexyard/*.json` inside the attested scope (lines 11–18), which is exactly what the `isBundlePath` fix in this same range removed — confirming the bundle predates the fix and was never regenerated. Net effect: the one artifact this PR exists to ship is invalid as committed, and the required `CI` check goes red on every push.
findings.summary: Committed bundle describes HEAD~1 and a failing review, so the Evidence bundle gate fails

findings.detail: When `verify-evidence.mjs` already passes for this content the review is skipped (`skip_stage "1. ApexYard AI review (already attested for this content)"`), but that branch sets none of `SKIP_REVIEW` / `NOTHING_TO_PUSH` / `REVIEW_QUALIFIED`, so the guard at line 216 does not fire and stages 10 and 11 run anyway. Stage 10 runs `node scripts/evidence.mjs`, which reads the review output from `.apexyard/review/review.json` — gitignored (`.gitignore:28`), so absent in a fresh clone or after `git clean -xdf`. `collectReview(null)` and `collectFindings(null)` then return `available: false`, `evidence.mjs` overwrites the valid committed `review.json` and `findings.json` with unavailable payloads, and stage 11 fails with "review.json reports the review did not run — an unrun review is not a passing one". The reachable flow is ordinary: clone, then `git push origin HEAD:some-branch`, where the pre-push hook picks a merge-base the committed attestation already covers. The gate blocks the push and leaves a degraded bundle in the tree; recovery is `git checkout .apexyard`, which is not obvious from the error.
findings.summary: "Already attested" skip still regenerates the bundle, clobbering it with available:false

findings.detail: `observed` and `pagesScanned` are module-level, and `test.afterAll` runs once per worker process, not once per file. `playwright.config.ts:17` sets `fullyParallel: true` and `:30` sets `workers: 4` on CI (CPU count locally), so the five scanning tests in this file are distributed across workers. Each worker imports its own copy of the module, accumulates only the scans it ran, and then writes the full `test-results/axe-summary.json` — last writer wins. `accessibility-report.json` therefore under-reports `violations_total` and `pages_scanned`, and does so differently depending on which worker finishes last. Two consequences specific to this design: the bundle stops being reproducible across runs even though nothing changed (the determinism guard cannot see this — the values are stable-shaped, just incomplete), and because `verify-local.sh` regenerates the bundle on every push, the tree goes dirty with a fresh `accessibility-report.json` each time, producing an endless "refresh evidence bundle" commit loop. It is also the same "absence reads as success" failure the collectors were built to prevent, one layer out: fewer violations look like fewer violations, not like a partial scan.
findings.summary: afterAll runs per worker, so axe-summary.json records only one worker's subset

findings.detail: gitattributes resolves conflicts by giving precedence to the **last** matching line. `*  text=auto` on line 22 matches every path, so for the `text` attribute it overrides the earlier per-path rules — including `.apexyard/attestation.sig  -text` on line 20, whose comment says "`-text` on the signature keeps git from touching it at all." The signature ends up back under `text=auto` eol normalisation. The practical exposure is small (an `ssh-keygen -Y sign` output is ASCII-armoured, so `text=auto` detects it as text and LF is what both ends want), which is why this is low rather than higher — it becomes a real verification failure only if the signature format ever gains a byte git would rewrite. The `eol=lf` pins on lines 3–19 survive, since line 22 sets only `text`.
findings.summary: Catch-all text=auto is last, so it overrides -text on attestation.sig

findings.detail: `json.filter(…).map((f) => toPosixRelative(f.filePath, root)).sort().length` builds an array of relative paths, sorts it, and discards it — only the count reaches the payload. The `map` and `sort` are dead work, and they are the only reason `collectEslint` takes a `root` parameter at all, which makes the signature look like it produces paths. On a run with many flagged files it also does needless per-file path normalisation. If the paths were meant to be emitted (the sort strongly suggests so), the artifact is silently missing a field the code was written to produce.
findings.summary: files_with_findings maps and sorts a list only to read its length

findings.detail: Lines 128–129 state "Skipping this file is not cosmetic: it necessarily contains every pattern it searches for, so including it guarantees a self-match", and line 153 states "Skipping the pattern-list lines themselves, now that the file is in scope." Neither behaviour exists in the code — `list_scan_targets` has no exclusion — and both directly contradict lines 102–109, which explain at length that the file is deliberately in scope because `[` immediately follows each prefix so no pattern matches itself. On a security-relevant script the cost is real: a reader auditing whether the scanner has a blind spot will find a comment asserting the exact blind spot the code was changed to remove, and may "restore" it.
findings.summary: Comments claim the scanner skips itself, contradicting the block that says it must not

findings.detail: `npx eslint . -f json -o "$RAW/eslint.json"` writes the machine-readable capture, then `npm run lint --silent` runs `eslint .` again purely to obtain an exit code. On this repo that is two full lints of every `.ts`/`.tsx` in the pre-push path, and the header comment already names the reason the second run exists (`|| true` on the first would hide the exit status). The two runs also read the tree at slightly different moments, so in principle the gated result and the captured evidence can disagree — the exact property the surrounding comment ("the evidence is a record of the run that actually gated, not a re-run") says the design is trying to guarantee.
findings.summary: lint_and_capture runs ESLint over the whole repo twice

findings.detail: Line 18 sets `"baseUrl": "."`, and lines 19–21 immediately below say "No baseUrl: it is deprecated in TS 6 and removed in 7. Since TS 4.x, \"paths\" resolves relative to this file when baseUrl is absent." One of the two is wrong, and the comment reads as the intended end state that was not carried out. No functional impact today — `baseUrl: "."` plus a repo-relative `paths` entry resolves identically — but the next reader has to decide which line to trust, and the deprecation the comment warns about will land as a build failure on a TS major bump that the comment claims was already handled.
findings.summary: baseUrl is set directly above a comment stating it was removed
